chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is there a specific time/limit for recitation in the prayer?' He said, 'No, except for Friday, where Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun are recited.'

I said to him, 'Then which Surahs are recited in the prayers?' He said, 'As for Dhuhr and the last Isha, they are recited equally (with the same Surahs), and Asr and Maghrib are equal (with the same Surahs).
And as for the morning (Fajr), it is longer. And as for Dhuhr and the last Isha - [recite] 'Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High' and 'By the sun and its brightness' and similar ones.
And as for Asr and Maghrib - [recite] 'When the victory of Allah has come' and 'Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you' and similar ones.

And as for the morning (Fajr) - [recite] 'About what are they asking one another?', 'Has there reached you the news of the Overwhelming?', 'I swear by the Day of Resurrection', and 'Has there come upon man a period of time from the past?'

key_terms.أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ: Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you (Surah At-Takathur)
key_terms.إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ: When the victory of Allah has come (Surah An-Nasr)
key_terms.سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَى: Glory be to the name of your Lord, the Most High (Surah Al-A'la)
key_terms.عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ: About what are they asking one another (Surah An-Naba)

ai.seo_question: Which Surahs should be recited in each of the five daily prayers according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific Surahs recommended by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) for the five daily prayers, establishing a structured hierarchy of recitation length that reflects the spiritual gravity of each time. It highlights the distinction between the longer, more contemplative recitations for Fajr and the concise, impactful verses for Dhuhr and Isha, while reserving specific Surahs for the congregational Friday prayer. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' practical guidance in worship, balancing brevity with profound theological themes.
